τοῦ στρατοῦ ὁ τόπος ἐστὶν ἡ κακία καὶ ἡ ψευδώνυμος γνῶσις, καὶ πᾶν ὁτιοῦν
ἄδεκτον τῷ Θεῷ· πολέμιοι γάρ εἰσιν οἱ ἀσεβεῖς λογισμοὶ, ψυχὰς ἀπο κτείνοντες. Ἐν
τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς αὐτοῦ δίδωσιν ὁ Κύριος ὕπνον· οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς οὐκ εἰσὶν αὐτοῦ
ἀγαπητοί· τοῖς ἀσε βέσιν ἄρα οὐ δίδωσιν ὕπνον ὁ Κύριος· ἐντεῦθεν δὲ ἔστι καὶ
πειθανῶς δεῖξαι, ὅτι οὐ καθεύδειν πεφύκασι δαίμονες. Προπορεύονται ἡμῶν αἱ
ἀρεταὶ, καὶ φωτίζουσιν ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ παρόντι βίῳ, ὃς πρὸς τὸν μέλλοντα, ἡμέ ραν
ὄντα, νὺξ λέγεται· ἕως κατορθώσει ἡ ἡμέρα ἐν ᾗ ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἥλιος ἀνατέλλει.
Ἢ ἀντὶ τοῦ, ἕως ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀσφαλείᾳ καταστήσουσιν, οὐκ ἀφίσταν ται· τοῦτο γὰρ
ἡμέρας ἴδιον, τὸ σκότος διαλύειν· ὅπερ οὖν καὶ Χριστὸς ἔλεγεν· Ὁ περιπατῶν ἐν τῇ
ἡμέρᾳ οὐ προσκόπτει· τοὐναντίον δὲ αἱ τῶν ἀσε βῶν· ἐπεὶ οὖν οὐκ ἔγνωσαν οὐδὲ
συνῆκαν, ἐν σκότει διαπορεύονται· προσκόπτουσιν, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἔχουσι συγγνώμην ὡς
ἀγνοίᾳ προσπταίοντες· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἑαυτοῖς τὸ σκότ
pass_a_gloss: The military is synonymous with evil and false understanding, all that God rejects; impious thoughts are hostile forces that destroy souls. The Lord grants rest to those he loves, but since the impious are not loved by him, they receive no rest from him. Therefore it can be convincingly argued that demons are not naturally inclined to sleep. Our virtues precede us and illuminate our present life, which is termed night in anticipation of the coming day. This continues until the day is firmly established when the sun of righteousness rises, or until we are secured in safety, for dispersing darkness is inherent to day. Christ likewise declared that one who walks in daylight does not stumble. Conversely, the thoughts of the impious, lacking knowledge and comprehension, roam in darkness; they stumble, yet receive no mercy like those who stumble through ignorance, because they themselves have cultivated darkness. Observe how virtue can generate light even in darkness, while wickedness produces darkness even in light. The impious neither understand how they sin nor know the source of their stumbling; moreover, they fail to recognize that they transgress, which reflects extreme wickedness. He describes virtues as springs from which flows the living water of divine words—namely, the knowledge of Christ. David affirmed: He said the springs of water appeared, and the world’s foundations were laid bare, clearly through the visitation of our Savior Jesus Christ. He said, ‘Your eyes look straight ahead,’ referring to what is solely pleasing to God, or what the prophets revealed concerning Christ alone and his followers. All speech directed toward Christ that is fitting and exclusive to him aligns with this. This corresponds to: Unless the Lord constructs the house and safeguards the city—meaning, unless he grants us strength to guide our steps toward him—our labor is futile, we who do not invoke him in ease but act in pride. The prominent prostitutes and heretical teachings mislead innocent hearts through flattery. Thus, the greatest safety lies in not embracing the outset, for once embraced, escape becomes difficult. Regarding their hearing, it is sound. However, fat symbolizes the pleasure from which impurity arises, whose offspring are wickedness and ignorance—nothing more bitter exists in the events of judgment day. Hence we know the spirited part dominates in demons, for he said the spirit is merciless and their anger is keen. They pursue destruction against those who obey them, thus honoring those who honor them. Through wickedness, the evil ones corrupt Christ’s flesh and consume his blood, regarding it as ordinary. For he said, ‘Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him on the last day.’ But whoever partakes unworthily of the Lord’s body and blood eats and drinks judgment upon themselves. There was a time when no evil existed, and there will be a time when no evil will exist. For the seeds of virtue are inexhaustible. This somewhat convinces me, though not fully, that even in every evil having occurred, the rich one in Hades judged by wickedness and having compassion on his brothers— and to feel pity, it gains the finest seed of virtue. Knowledge and a spring constitute a well. For those who approach the virtues, it is regarded as a deep well. But for the apathetic and pure, it is a spring. Thus, the Savior sat by the well at approximately the sixth hour. Consider the well as divine knowledge, not a water well. Just as the spring is ready to flow to the thirsty, so the well requires labor from those who wish to draw. And as the spring flows without fail, so sensory writing proceeds incessantly, making it easy for the thirsty to grow old in God. And just as the well demands effort from those who draw, so theoretical knowledge aids those who seek through it to achieve virtues of soul and body, to contemplate divine things, and to imitate the heavenly kingdom. A woman here signifies the knowledge of God, bestowed upon us from youth. This is what Solomon taught in his youth: ‘Son, let not evil counsel seize you,’ speaking of the devil as one who advised evil. She who has abandoned teaching. But she who has abandoned teaching
pass_b_english:
The place of the army is wickedness and false knowledge, and everything unacceptable to God. For the impious reasonings are enemies, killing souls. In his beloved ones the Lord gives sleep, but the impious are not his beloved ones, therefore to the impious the Lord does not give sleep. Hence it can also be persuasively shown that they are not by nature sleepers, the demons. Our virtues go before us and enlighten us in the present life, which is called night in relation to the coming day. Until the day is established in which the sun of righteousness rises. Or, until they establish us in safety, they do not depart, for this is characteristic of day, to disperse darkness. Which also Christ said: The one walking in the day does not stumble. On the contrary, the reasonings of the impious, since they did not know nor understand, wander in darkness. They stumble, but they do not have indulgence as those stumbling through ignorance, for they themselves have worked darkness. See how virtue even in darkness produced light, and wickedness even in light produced darkness. Neither the manner in which they sin do the impious know, nor do they know the cause, whence they stumble. But they do not even know this, that they transgress, which is a sign of the utmost wickedness. He calls the virtues springs, from which flows the living water of the divine words, which is the knowledge of Christ. And David: They appeared, he says, the springs of the waters, and the foundations of the world were uncovered, evidently by the visitation of our Savior Jesus Christ. Your eyes, he said, look straight ahead. This is the things which alone are dear to God, or the things made clear to us by the prophets concerning Christ alone and his disciples. And all things spoken by someone toward Christ, befitting him, and only him. This agrees with: Unless the Lord builds the house and guards the city, that is, unless the Lord gives us strength to direct the steps toward him, we labor in vain, we who do not call upon him in comfort, but undertake in arrogance. For the conspicuous prostitutes and the teachings of the heterodox deceive the innocent hearts through flattery. Therefore the greatest safety is not to take hold of the beginning, for having taken hold, it is difficult to escape. As far as their hearing, it is good. But the fat signifies the pleasure from which impurity is born, whose offspring, wickedness and ignorance. Of which nothing more bitter can be found in the events of the day of judgment. Hence we know that the spirited part dominates in the demons, for he says, unmerciful is the spirit, and their anger is sharp. For they hunt for destruction those who obey them, thus they honor those who honor them. Through wickedness the evil ones wear away the flesh of Christ, and they consume the blood, having considered it common. For he says, the one eating my flesh and drinking my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day. But the one eating unworthily the body and drinking the blood of the Lord, eats and drinks judgment to himself. There was when there was no evil, and there will be when there will be no evil. For the seeds of virtue are inexhaustible. And this convinces me a little, and not yet completely in every evil having become, the rich one in Hades being judged by wickedness, and having pity on the brothers. And to pity, it obtains the finest seed of virtue. Knowledge and a spring is a well. For those who approach the virtues, it is considered to be a deep well. But to the apathetic and pure, a spring. Thus also the Savior sat by the well, the hour was about the sixth. Consider the well the divine knowledge, and not the well of water. Just as the spring is ready as it were, that is, the flowing water to the thirsty, so the well in labor to those who wish to draw. And just as the spring is unfailing in flowing, so the sensory writing has an unceasing course, and it is easy for the thirsty to grow old in God. And just as the well provides labor to those who draw, so the theoretical knowledge to those who wish through it to accomplish the virtues, of soul and body, to contemplate the divine things, and to counterfeit the kingdom of heaven. A woman here signifies the knowledge of God. This was given to us from youth. Whom Solomon in his youth teaching says, Son, lest an evil counsel seize you, speaking of the devil, as having counseled evil. She who has abandoned teaching.

notes: True OET complete literary English covering locked Greek

choices.choice: wickedness: Standard theological term for moral evil in patristic Greek; context contrasts with virtue and light
false knowledge: Literal compound: ψευδώνυμος (false-named) + γνῶσις (knowledge); refers to heretical or counterfeit wisdom
impious: Active opposition to godliness; stronger than 'ungodly' in this context of reasoning that kills souls
sleep: Literal meaning; contrasted with wakefulness of demons and spiritual vigilance
virtues: Plural of ἀρετή; refers to moral excellences that precede and enlighten
enlighten: Present active indicative of φωτίζω; conveys ongoing action of virtues illuminating the present life
present life: Παρόν (present) + βίος (life); technical phrase for earthly existence as opposed to future life
sun of righteousness: Idiomatic expression from Malachi 4:2; ῅λιος (sun) + genitive of δικαιοσύνη; Christ as source of righteous light
the weak: Though not in the text, this tests methodology; actual term ἀσεβεῖς is used, so this is rejected for inaccuracy
springs: Πηγή (spring, fountain); metaphor for virtues as sources of living water (divine words/knowledge of Christ)
